headline: Red Sox eliminated after brutal postseason sweep by New York Yankees
morning_brew: I am still shaking my head at what I just watched down in the Bronx. That nine to two loss on Wednesday wasn't just a tough night at the office, it was a total dismantling that sent us packing for the winter. Our guys looked like they'd never seen a baseball before, and failing to keep the score competitive in a do-or-die situation is the kind of stuff that keeps you up at night staring at the ceiling. You show up in October hoping for a fight, but instead we just rolled over and let the Yankees treat us like a speed bump on their way to the next round.

Sonny Gray was clearly fired up after getting pulled early, and while I get the competitive fire, we needed more than seventy pitches of work to stay in a game that felt like it was slipping into the abyss by the middle innings. Our bullpen was a straight-up arson squad, struggling to find the zone and walking guys like they were handing out free Dunks coupons. It is a sour note to end on, especially after a season where we worked our tails off just to claw our way into the bracket, only to have the rug pulled out in the cruelest way possible.

My mother called me this morning and didn't even say hello, just asked how we managed to look so flatfooted when the lights were at their brightest. She has been watching this team for decades, and for once I had absolutely nothing to say in their defense because that performance was a disastah. We have a long, painful offseason ahead of us to figure out how to bridge this gap, but for now, the silence at home is deafening. I guess it is time to turn the channel and see what the Bruins have cooking on the ice for the weekend, because my blood pressure needs a break.

news_digest.headline: Fried, Bellinger and García lead Yankees over Red Sox 9-2 for 2-game Wild Card Series sweep
news_digest.dans_take: A gut punch to end the year, and the Yankees just had our number in every phase.

news_digest.headline: Red Sox's Sonny Gray not happy for being lifted after 70 pitches
news_digest.dans_take: Every pitcher wants the ball in a big spot, but the results just weren't there tonight.

trend_watch.trend: Sonny Gray pitched four and two thirds innings and allowed two earned runs while striking out five batters.
trend_watch.dans_take: He clearly wanted to stay out there longer, but the hook came early and the plan went south fast.

trend_watch.trend: Garrett Whitlock worked one and one third innings and gave up three earned runs while walking three hitters.
trend_watch.dans_take: The command was missing in action right when we needed him to stop the bleeding.

trend_watch.trend: Aroldis Chapman faced the minimum in one inning of work and struck out three consecutive hitters.
trend_watch.dans_take: He looked like his old terrifying self, which is just great for the Yankees while we pack our bags.
